sentences.text: Jeyawati is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur whose name translates to "grinding mouth" in the Zuni language.
The type species, Jeyawati rugoculus, was formally described in 2010 based on fossils found in New Mexico.
This animal is known from an incomplete skeleton consisting of disarticulated skull parts and fragmentary postcranial bones.
The species is distinguished by a rough texture on the side of the postorbital bone and a large opening at the base of its jugal process.
The species name refers to its chewing adaptations and the wrinkled texture of the bone around the eye.
Jeyawati possessed primitive features in its teeth and jaws alongside characteristics of the hadrosauroid lineage.
Fossils of Jeyawati rugoculus were discovered in 1996 in the Moreno Hill Formation in western New Mexico.
The holotype specimen was found by Douglas G. Wolfe, Hazel Wolfe, and Christopher Wolfe during the Zuni Basin Paleontological Project.
Excavation and collection of the specimen continued for about 13 years with help from James I. Kirkland and volunteers.
Andrew T. McDonald, Douglas G. Wolfe, and James I. Kirkland formally described the species in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology in 2010.
A cladistic analysis indicates Jeyawati was more primitive than Shuangmiaosaurus, Telmatosaurus, and Bactrosaurus, but more advanced than Eolambia, Probactrosaurus, and Protohadros.
Jeyawati belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
The genus authority is cited as Wolfe & Kirkland, 2010.
Jeyawati lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Jeyawati lived in North America approximately 97 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
The time range for Jeyawati is estimated between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
